results.note: ingest-medium.yml mirrors ingest.yml's structure: same trigger shape (schedule/workflow_dispatch/push paths), permissions: contents: read, timeout-minutes: 10, checkout/setup-python/setup-uv steps, and `uv run python -m ingest.heartbeat --tier <tier>` invocation — only cron string, job name, and heartbeat secret name differ.

The diff touches zero lines of ingest/pipeline.py or ingest/registry.py; the workflow only adds `--tier medium` to the already-existing heartbeat CLI, which routes into US-1201's unmodified tier filter.

Research doc explicitly cites Healthchecks.io's own documented 'one check per job' practice with a link (10-research.md:20); implementation matches it with a dedicated `HEALTHCHECK_URL_INGEST_MEDIUM` secret distinct from the daily and canary checks, asserted by the new workflow test.

Attempt 2 added a genuine end-to-end test that calls heartbeat.main(['--tier','medium']) directly, mocking only I/O boundaries (psycopg.connect, httpx.get, and each vendor fetcher, with non-funding fetchers set to raise if called) and asserting the real pipeline persists exactly the 4 medium funding-rate rows and pings once. This is the same pattern already accepted for the daily tier in US-1202 and closes the gap the attempt-1 verdict correctly flagged.

No evidence anywhere in the repo (events.ndjson, SESSION.md, gates) of an actual completed or dispatched GitHub Actions run of ingest-medium.yml — only a static YAML-text test exists. This is the identical structural gap US-1202-C5 had, which was only closed there by a human manually running `gh workflow run ingest.yml` and citing the resulting run URL/conclusion; no equivalent remediation (run URL, dispatch log) is present for ingest-medium.yml.
Gate result 'US-1203-C6: exit 0 [uv run pytest -q]' confirms the full offline suite passes on current HEAD, including the new medium-tier integration test.
